# Actually, we can reuse the elementwise addition pattern but for matmul we need nested loops.
# Let's implement a simple kernel that performs standard matrix multiplication using two-level loops.

elementmatmul_source = """
#include <torch/extension.h>
#include <cuda_runtime.h>

// Kernel: C = A @ B
// Inputs:
//   A: shape (M, K)
//   B: shape (K, N)
//   C: output shape (M, N)
__global__ void matmul_kernel(const float* A, const float* B, float* C, int M, int K, int N) {
    // Each thread computes one element C[i][j].
    int idx = blockIdx.x * blockDim.x + threadIdx.x;
    if (idx < M * N) {
        int i = idx / N;
        int j = idx % N;
        float sum = 0.0f;
        // Loop over k
        for (int k = 0; k < K; ++k) {
            sum += A[i * K + k] * B[k * N + j];
        }
        C[idx] = sum;
    }
}

torch::Tensor matmul_cuda(torch::Tensor A, torch::Tensor B) {
    // Determine dimensions
    int M = A.size(0);
    int K = A.size(1);
    int N = B.size(1);

    auto out = torch::empty({M, N}, A.dtype(), torch::Device::cuda);
    // Launch kernel
    const int block_size = 256;
    const int num_blocks = (M * N + block_size - 1) / block_size;
    matmul_kernel<<<num_blocks, block_size>>>(

        B.data_ptr<float>(),
        out.data_ptr<float>(),

    return out;
